thread:
Noah (new-hire): hey team, day 2 here. using the split-tunnel WireGuard profile and SSHing to bastion-us-east. sessions freeze after ~6-8m and sometimes gitlab host looks unresolved. anyone got quick debugging tips?

Ivy (infra): welcome! super common with macOS + split-tunnel. two quick checks: 1) add ServerAliveInterval to ssh config; 2) ensure WireGuard DNS points to our internal resolver. can you paste your Host entry?

Noah (new-hire): here's my ~/.ssh/config:

```
Host bastion-us-east
  HostName bastion.us-east-1.redwood
  User noah
  ProxyCommand ssh -W %h:%p jump.redwood
```

Sam (it-support): on mac the system resolver can flip to the ISP when interfaces re-prioritize. If WG isn't forcing DNS, git pushes will fail with "Could not resolve host". Try setting DNS in the WG profile to 10.0.2.2 and make AllowedIPs include 10.0.0.0/8.

Ivy (infra): also replace ProxyCommand with ProxyJump and add these lines:

```
  ServerAliveInterval 25
  ServerAliveCountMax 3
  TCPKeepAlive yes
```

Noah (new-hire): added ProxyJump + ServerAliveInterval and set WG DNS to 10.0.2.2. Still saw one hang during a maintenance notice.

deploy-bot: scheduled maintenance: bastion-us-east-2 rebooting in 10m (maint-2026-06-01-4) :warning:

Ivy (infra): if you were routed to the host being rebooted you'd see a drop. The DNS flaps are a separate issue; forcing internal DNS in the WG client usually fixes it. If you can't edit the profile, add an /etc/resolver/redwood file pointing to 10.0.2.2 as a short-term workaround.

Noah (new-hire): creating /etc/resolver/redwood fixed git resolution. after switching to ProxyJump and ServerAliveInterval the SSH session stayed up for 45m. thanks!

Sam (it-support): welcome aboard! we'll update the new-hire WG profile to pin DNS and include the gitlab subnet. I'll add a short line to the onboarding doc about macOS resolver quirks.

Noah (new-hire): huge help, appreciated :raised_hands:
